title: A Moth Flies 600 Miles by the Stars to a Cave It Has Never Seen

scenes.text: This moth flies 600 miles by the stars. To a place it has never seen.
Every spring, Australia's bogong moths leave the lowlands and fly up to a thousand kilometers to cool caves in the Alps.
Each moth makes the trip once. Its parents died long before. Nobody shows it the way.
In 2025, scientists tethered moths under a projected night sky and switched off Earth's magnetic field around them.
The moths steered by the stars. Rotate the sky, and they turned with it. Scramble it, and they were lost.
Under cloud they switched to a magnetic compass. The first insect ever shown to navigate by the stars.

description:
A moth that flies up to 1,000 kilometers by the stars to a cave it has never seen.
Each spring, Australia's bogong moths migrate from the lowlands to cool caves in the Australian Alps; every moth makes the journey once, long after its parents have died. In a 2025 Nature study, Lund University researchers tethered moths under a projected night sky with Earth's magnetic field cancelled out: the moths steered by the stars, turned when the sky was rotated, and lost their way when it was scrambled. On cloudy nights they fell back on a magnetic compass. It is the first invertebrate shown to use the stars for long-distance navigation.
Which animal migration amazes you most?
subject: bogong moth
first_comment: The moths spend the summer dormant in the caves and fly all the way back in autumn to breed and die. What other animal finds its way somewhere it has never been?
